messages:
oncall_bot: [ALERT] spike in 5xx + OOM events on serving-runtime-gpu pool. Auto-detected: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS in multiple containers. Triage channel opened.

alex_r: seeing repeated stack traces like `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` + container restart loop on pods serving large-context models. node gpu-14 flapped 3x. attaching sample log excerpt.

alex_r: ```
E 02:13:45 container#1234 runtime: cuda: illegal memory access at 0x7f3a2c..
E 02:13:45 k8s: pod serving-runtime-xyz restarted (OOM killed)
E 02:13:46 nvml: driver reported ECC? false
```

sre_jordan: cordoning gpu-14 now and starting drain. moving live traffic off node. will scale up warm spare pool. :mega:

ml_infra: preliminary correlation: incidents started after kernel+driver batch deployed ~01:12 UTC (nvidia driver 520.61 + kernel 5.10.3 patch). reproducer shows misaligned deviceaddr during pagewalk under concurrent mmap + eviction. looks like a kernel-driver race.

ops_lee: cgroup memory pressure seen on some pods prior to illegal access. sequence: mem spike -> OOM kill -> subsequent illegal access on restart (kv cache warmup?). need to prevent noisy restarts.

eng_lead_maya: list of hosts with the rollout? we should stop rollout and freeze updates. schedule rollback if needed.

alex_r: hosts with driver 520.61: gpu-14, gpu-17, gpu-23. rollout paused. preparing emergency rollback to 519.85 on affected nodes.

oncall_bot: Estimated customer impact: ~3 production customers affected, ~1.8% of global requests returned 5xx, p95 latency +350-450ms for some tenants during failover. streams aborted for long-context generative workloads.

cust_success_sam: notifying customers now — A and B on watch, C receiving degraded latency. messaging note: "temporary reroute to smaller models + retry" recommended.

sre_jordan: mitigation steps applied: 1) cordon+drain gpu-14/gpu-17, 2) enable serving fallback routing to redwood-small for high-QPS routes, 3) increase cache TTL temporarily to reduce kv warmups, 4) suspend autoscaler from scheduling new pods onto kernel-updated hosts.

ml_infra: rolling a conservative hotfix: set ENV DISABLE_PMA=1 in serving runtime to avoid a recently added prefetch path that touches device addr ranges during cold start. patch push ongoing.

alex_r: if hotfix fails, plan B = driver rollback -> restart kubelet -> recreate pods. coordinating with infra to stagger so we don't mass-migrate traffic.

eng_lead_maya: create a dedicated trace bundle and attach to incident ticket. collect: /var/log/serving/*.log, nvml debug, dmesg, and kernel oops. keep it for postmortem.

ml_infra: uploaded traces to s3://redwood-incidents/1809998887/trace.tgz and created diagnostic gist for kernel oops. linking in ticket.

ops_lee: starting controlled driver rollback on gpu-17 (non-customer critical) as canary. will monitor for recurrence for 15m before wider rollback.

alex_r: canary looked good so far (10m). no new illegal access on gpu-17 after rollback.

eng_lead_maya: handoff summary for night oncall @sre_jordan: hotfix applied (DISABLE_PMA=1), rollback plan in place, 2 nodes rolled back successfully. still monitoring. escalate to SEV2 if customer error rate >5% or leak recurs.

oncall_bot: Incident tagged SEV2. If not resolved in 6h please open postmortem and include timeline + kernel/driver diff + remediation plan. :memo:

sre_jordan: taking over monitoring and customer comms. I'll update every 30m or on any regression. :white_check_mark:
